links.outcome: Physician-perceived skill degradation and technical dependency from digital-intelligent medical technology
links.effect: Interviewed physicians described technical dependency and skill degradation risks as new job demands; no prevalence figures reported.
links.quote: Challenges such as technical dependency, operational complexity, and ethical responsibility arising from digital-intelligent medical technologies impose new job demands on physicians, exacerbating burnout and skill degradation risks.

links.outcome: Physician-perceived job demands, burnout and efficiency effects of AI tools
links.effect: Technologies were perceived to improve efficiency and decision accuracy, but also added operational complexity and burnout risk; qualitative only, no quantified effects.
links.quote: Challenges such as technical dependency, operational complexity, and ethical responsibility arising from digital-intelligent medical technologies impose new job demands on physicians, exacerbating burnout and skill degradation risks.

unlisted_practices: Liability insurance for physicians using AI
Regional data sharing to reduce resource disparities between hospitals

screen.reason: Qualitative study exploring physicians' experiences and perceptions of using various AI and digital-intelligent technologies in clinical practice and how it affects their job demands and resources.
